FUN (but challenging) game. Very interesting story, right up until the end. The end is a kind of.... "meh, it's over". 

Hoping for a sequel with more storyline.

[b]July 29th update[/b]: Chasing the achievements, I finished New Game++ and that was the first time the game was actually fun. When I acquired gear and upgraded my stats to the point that I could deal with the incessant amount of poorly designed enemies the game keeps throwing at you at some reasonable rate. Even then, some places and enemy combinations were really terrible, just further revealing the bad design choices.

Immortal: Chained in Crumminess or as it's affectionately called "Enter from the Back Simulator, but They're Kind of Shy" is an overly ambitious undertaking from a small indie studio with a terribly implemented souls formula adding guns into the mix, amazing bugs still present even after 2 years and a DLC, a parody of an AI, poor combat with bad hitboxes, weird and glitchy enemy and character animations, dreadful enemy placements and combinations, general floatiness and slowness of everything and an aggressively hostile attitude towards players, wasting their time and fundamentally and completely missing the point of what makes Dark Souls great.

Absolutely nothing this game does well, level designs and visuals, incredible shortcuts and the connectedness of zones, great lore and a fun way it's served to you, through a bit of story, different pickups and enemy drops, various weapons and an interesting upgrade mechanic, a great idea for upgrading armour through finding armour shrines, tough, but good boss fights, a giant amount of secrets and extra areas, a good ending, none of that redeems the game in any sensible way from the utter garbage not even worthy of recycling that are this game's combat mechanics, gameplay and AI. It's astoundingly bad, ill-thought-out and shows a great lack of knowledge of what makes good soulslikes hard, but fair and fun. The DLC doesn't improve anything, it makes things worse with broken enemies that come in droves and the most unfair boss fight you'll encounter.

Enemy animations and behaviour is very glitchy, sometimes getting them stuck on random pieces of scenery and sometimes making them spot you from miles away and firing or running at you. The enemies are very often chain triggered together, even drawing enemies from incredible distances. There are a couple of enemies that charge you and that running attack animation is horrendous, they just explode into a charge like a dragster car and the hitbox on that is particularly terrible, as are hitboxes on most melee attacks. A lot of enemies don't really have any hints or tells for their ranged attacks and some of the attacks are hitscan, making them very hard to avoid. Your melee attacks are just two slow, lousy swings. They can be chained depending on the weapon, but it's mostly useless. Your ranged attacks don't use stamina, melee and your dodge does, but a lot of enemy attacks stun you or knock you down even at a full stamina bar. That usually gets you instantly killed. Enemies are frequently placed in hard to reach spots, behind shields or on high ground, backed by melee enemies that spawn when you approach, making you backtrack and leaving you with no other option but to go slow and run out of ammo. There are instances when the enemies silently spawn behind you when you're already engaging multiple other enemies. The main idea is to shoot enemies in the back where they have weak spots, but it doesn't work well due to enemy animations, hitbox problems, awfully bad placements and the sheer amount of enemies. The further you are in the game, the worse all these problems become since the game throws harder and harder enemies at you, but doesn't reduce the numbers. And it's a game with guns. What's the point of guns that do laughable damage from the front when you have to go in close, sidestep and shoot from point blank in the back? And there are obnoxious teleporting enemies reused over and over. Someone somewhere at one of the gameplay meetings said "You know what? We haven't done enough mind-bogglingly bad design choices, guys and girls! We need enemies with hitscan/sticky grenade/oneshot instant knockdown weapons that teleport! Dooooo iiiiiit!".

There's a lot more to tell here if I include multiple bugs still present in the game after 2 years, enemies getting knocked out of bounds, not dying but continuing to track you through the level and firing at you, sometimes unreachable, but always annoying trash mobs spawned by bosses, one horrendous type of phasing/teleporting melee enemy, constant lack of ammunition, ankle high elevations that your character cannot traverse and a ton of other bad choices, but there's not enough space in a Steam review for everything. The gameplay and the entire combat system are extremely cheap, badly thought out and flawed by design. Napoleon's invasion of Russia in 1812 was better thought out than this. Dark Souls with guns this is not.

The level designs are good, but not made for ranged combat, featuring many cramped spaces where the game continues to throw multiple enemies at you. That you need to shoot in the back. What the effing flying fudge!? There are plenty of guns to choose from, the weapon upgrade system is interesting, but the gun requirements linking them to stats is messed up and too harsh. All the guns don't really have much range and there's a significant damage drop off, effectively gimping the gun combat even further. There are various items that give different buffs and resistances, but they're not really that useful.

I would love to say that patience is a virtue in this game, go grind and git gud, to use the mind numbing phrase soulslikes elitists love, but the combat mechanics here are so excruciatingly bad and shoddy that even grinding for stats and gear isn't much help in the long run. It just makes the game less tedious, if you have the patience for it. It's a great vision by Toadman Interactive in almost every other aspect, but it impales itself on it's own Crusader Sword with frightfully bad gameplay and not respecting the player. This entire text could be replaced with a single sentence. If you want a shooter soulslike, go play [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/617290/Remnant_From_the_Ashes/][b]Remnant: From the Ashes[/b][/url]. It's also not perfect, but miles better than this poorly cobbled Monolith.  

Take a peek inside the newly opened [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/thecabinetofcuriosities/discussions/0/2272575584124463561/][b]Cabinet of Curiosities[/b][/url] if you like to walk off the beaten path and only sometimes return to the main roads. You might find something worth exploring. And if you do, thank you for the visit.

This is one of the absolute worst, and simultaneously decent games I have played. I bought it back in 2020 and gave it about 6 hours and bounced off of it. I picked it up again in 2023 after I had just played Hellpoint and I was wondering if Immortal would be worth re-checking out. It took 12 hours for the game to really become fun to play. I checked the in-game clock when I started feeling mirth instead of anxiety and dread. This game has excellent worlds to explore, usually the opening area of any of the 3 areas is really milquetoast but once you push deep enough into the level you get to see some real love being put into it all. You can play as an absolute unit of character which is funny because I dumped absolutely no points into strength. Improving your armor is tied to exploration as you need to find armor shrines to unlock the next piece of gear, that is automatically applied. The enemy design is has some real cool lookers but there are a lot of stinkers. Basically every single unit has a weak point on their back, however there are a lot of the really obnoxious enemies that use shields that will be facing you almost always, getting to that weak point on normal fodder is a real chore. On the flip side most of the bosses you fight can be downed in 15 seconds on a sub-optimal build. The third major boss I had to fight I missed my first shot with the sniper rifle, he turned to look at where the shot hit the wall, exposing his weak point, and he died in 3 shots. It was insane, and it happened to multiple bosses. This sparks joy. This game has so much love, but it really needs so much more. While it is a lot like dark souls in how all the management of resources and power plays out, the scenario design is piss poor. 2 out of 3 encounters will have you walk into a room that is empty, there are no indicators of enemies looming. As soon as you kiss that invisible trigger they will either crawl out of solid concrete or literally materialize out of the atoms in the air. And while its fun to just curb stomp the battles after the fact when you're backtracking for whatever, the first time you hit these ganks can be immensely annoying and you can't really blame yourself for not having the clairvoyance to know that Scotty is beaming down 16 bad guys who can gut you like a fish. Another thing that is rough "Whoa buddy" is the poise system. When that thresh hold breaks you might as well go walk it off irl because your character will lie on the ground until the sun sets and rises again, and the enemy will just group up around you and kick you until you die. It's absolutely insane. I genuinely kind of hate this game a lot. However I dumped 27 hours into this one play through, beat the game. I guess I kind of love it too. When my build finally started picking up the slack, the paradigm shifted and I had this come to Monolith moment where I just understood. I also loved the twist at the end of the game, it made me laugh in the way that you would when you're way past exhausted and will accept anything. The npcs were surprisingly good too, good voice acting, love to hear it. I also really enjoyed the concept art cutscenes, some good art there. The soundtrack was also fantastic, with a lot of moody atmospheric music that for some reason kept reminding me of ME1's world exploration tracks, like Ilos too, that kind of vibe. 
I think there was maybe too much 1-1 Norse mythos being used, the realms and the story of Baldr come to mind as immediate examples. Build on that more. Also this version of Hela has the same operation going as the Hela in Too Human, where the dead became mechanized zombies with guns. Which if that's a reference that's fun. 
The DLC I am not a huge fan of. I like that it pushes you to use multiple elemental weapon types to defeat varied enemy types at one time, but the boss design is dog water. The first 2 are the same boss that can just stunlock you into the ground and they have no weak point that you can really fish for as well as an over abundance of large tanky enemies that use a shield that covers their whole body. Really doubling down on the bad enemy design. 

Anyways tl:dr, I think this game has a lot to offer if you can cope with how absolutely painful stretches of this game can really be.

I played this game a while ago on my friend's account and I really liked it. I picked it up in a sale for 15$ and it's absolutely worth this price. It is a good game imo, nothing special. I like the weapons, the music, the graphics are pretty good. There are some lags here and there but overall this is a solid game.

An interesting take on the soulslike genre.
It has a lot of the TooHuman atmosphere from the mythological standpoint.Not a lot of high budget cut-scenes and the graphics are decent ( it was developed by a small studio so that is understandable). Most of the lore comes in the form of collectables and let me tell you, there are a lot of those.
The game has a difficulty spike that borders the unfair after the first location and the bugs and hit detection
are an extra punishment on top of a masochistic experience as it is. Several times you will find yourself screaming at the monitor, "there is no way that that sniper just teleported behind me and got a clear shot after I rolled out of his sight behind a corner" while spitting and hyperventilating in anger and frustration but you might pick it up again to see if you can defeat the 5 mobs ,who can 1 shot kill you ,that spawn out of nowhere and seem to all use aim-bots.

With all of that I still finished the game but I can't say that I felt like the story went somewhere or that the game loop 
kept me going.

If you like impossible to beat games and have nerves of steel, get this and get to NG+ :)
The game is way to clunky and unfair most of the times. It has its charm and some neat ideas but if the gameplay is frustrating than nothing can save it... what a shame.
